data.narrative:
Verne is a Seed-stage frontier-tech company in Climate & Energy founded by Ted McKlveen, David Jaramillo, and Bav Roy, with $17.5M total raised to date. The sector peer set comprises one public comparable (LNZA) and eight private peers including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix.

Valuation analysis relies on a single applicable method due to data constraints. Stage-Progression triangulation, anchoring to the $17.5M total raised as a valuation proxy, applies a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of Seed-to-Series A advancement, yielding an implied valuation of $44M. A Peer-Median approach proved inapplicable: while eight same-sector peers exist in Climate & Energy, insufficient overlap exists at matching stage, adjacent stage, or similar valuation tier to support a robust median calculation without introducing noise.

The triangulated valuation range is $37M to $50M, with a median point of $44M. This reflects the constraints of early-stage frontier-tech valuation in a fragmented sector. Key uncertainties include the absence of narrow-set peer comparables at Seed stage, limiting ability to benchmark against direct peers, and reliance on a single methodological input. Stage-Progression methodology carries inherent sensitivity to assumed multipliers; actual next-round pricing will depend on market conditions, capital availability in climate tech, and Verne's interim progress on core technical and commercial milestones.
